author: Jocelyn Flores
title: Canutillo ISD teacher selected for prestigious history program - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores ,
1 hours ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) -- A Canutillo Independent School District educator was selected to participate in a prestigious national history institute.
Loudres Balderrama, a transition specialist, was chosen as one of 50 educators to take part in the Gilder Lehrman Summer Institute for Teachers at Marist University.
Loudres Balderrama. Photo courtesy of Canutillo Independent School District. According to Canutillo ISD, the institute is a prestigious professional learning program that focuses on the leadership and legacy of former President Franklin D. Roosevelt's administration during the Great Depression, the New Deal and World War II.
“Being selected for this institute was an incredible opportunity to learn from leading historians, collaborate with educators from across the country and bring new ideas back to our students and teachers in Canutillo ISD,” Balderrama, a Canutillo High School alumna and doctoral candidate in history, said. “My goal is to continue using evidence-based practices that help all students engage with history, think critically and see themselves as capable learners.”
Photos courtesy of Canutillo Independent School District. The program provides educators with a "deeper understanding" of how Roosevelt's policies transformed the U.S. and influenced the role of mordern government, Canutillo ISD said.
The educators also explored research-based instructional strategies, inquiry-based learning practices and classroom activities designed to increase student engagement and diverse learners.
"Balderrama’s participation reflects Canutillo ISD’s commitment to academic excellence, continuous professional growth and providing educators with opportunities to bring innovative learning strategies into classrooms across the district," Canutillo ISD said.
